alignment_diagnostics.note: LayerNorm is not rotation-invariant, so R2 < 1 is structural. pre_l0_ln applies ln1 before collecting activations so alignment is at the exact interface Q/K/V read from.

unaligned_transplant.description: seed0 L0H3 -> seed1 L0H1, no alignment

one_interface_aligned.description: seed0 L0H3 -> seed1 L0H1, single-rotation aligned (post-L0, corrected SVD)

two_interface_aligned.description: seed0 L0H3 -> seed1 L0H1, two-rotation aligned (R_in for Q/K/V, R_out for out_proj)

random_rotation_control.description: seed0 L0H3 rotated by random orthogonal matrix -> seed1 L0H1
random_rotation_control.hypothesis: should be equivalent to unaligned — random rotation is not informative

noncritical_donor_aligned.description: seed0 L0H0 (non-critical), two-interface aligned -> seed1 L0H1
noncritical_donor_aligned.hypothesis: alignment alone should not rescue a non-functional head

interpretation.conclusion: CIRCUITS ARE GENUINELY NON-PORTABLE. Two-interface alignment gain: -0.0130 — not meaningful. Non-portability is NOT a basis problem. The induction circuit in seed 0 is inseparable from its full weight context.
interpretation.layernorm_caveat: LayerNorm is not rotation-invariant. We align at ln1(pre_L0_residual) which is the exact interface Q/K/V read from — this is the theoretically correct alignment point. R2 < 1 reflects that the two models have genuinely different LN-transformed representations, not a bug in the alignment procedure.
